key_insight: MF-Diffuser makes offline multi-agent planning scalable by diffusing over trajectory distributions in Wasserstein space, using mean-field structure to approximate thousands of agents with strong theoretical guarantees.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical path to deploy offline MARL in large-scale engineered systems where joint-state planning is otherwise intractable, while preserving stability and performance bounds.
method: Lifts planning from joint trajectories to trajectory distributions in Wasserstein space.
Uses a value-weighted chaotic entropy objective to balance return maximization and generative fidelity.
Applies a hierarchical coarse-to-fine denoising strategy that grows the agent population progressively.
evidence_signal: On three mean-field RL benchmarks spanning stage games, sequential dynamics, and adversarial team competition, MF-Diffuser achieved the best return in most settings, especially with suboptimal offline data and at scales of N ≥ 10^3.
watch_item: The approach relies on mean-field assumptions and propagation-of-chaos behavior, so performance may degrade when agent interactions are highly non-exchangeable or the representative subset is poorly chosen.
paper_title: Mean-Field Diffuser: Scaling Offline MARL to Thousands of Agents
